Archival Dispatch: 16 Master Broadcasts Dated Across Carter Family Border Radio, Edward R. Murrow, Orson Welles, and Moon Over Morocco

Date: 2026-08-21
Author: radio index
Reading: 4 min
Tags: The Carter Family, Border Radio, XERA, Edward R Murrow, Buchenwald, Orson Welles, War Bonds, Willie Mays, Moon Over Morocco, Jack Flanders, Tales of Pacific Powerland, Yank Bandstand, Original Filenames
Raw Markdown

Batch 80 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 80 recovers and dates 16 historical broadcasts across country music foundations, broadcast journalism monuments, wartime rallies, binaural audio adventures, sports history, and northwestern regional folklore: 3 rare 1939 high-power Mexican border radio transcriptions from The Carter Family On Border Radio (A.P., Sara, and Maybelle Carter on XERA), Edward R. Murrow's devastating April 15, 1945 CBS report on the liberation of Buchenwald and his I Can Hear It Now series, Orson Welles delivering an urgent 1943 national war bond address, the Allied Military Government's May 4, 1945 resumption of Radio Hamburg, 3 chapters of Meatball Fulton's surreal stereo masterpiece Moon Over Morocco (ZBS, 1974), 3 Pacific Northwest historical legends narrated by Nelson Olmsted on Tales of Pacific Powerland (1953), Willie Mays' immortal 1954 catch on Greatest Sports Thrills, newsreel voice Ed Herlihy on Recollections at 30, and swing music on AFRS Yank Bandstand.

2. Edward R. Murrow & Orson Welles (1943–1948)

Monuments of wartime broadcasting and journalistic integrity:

Original Circulating Filename Canonical Title Verified Airdate Broadcast Substance
Murrow_Buchenwald_Liberation.mp3 "Edward R. Murrow: 'Eyewitness Report on the Liberation of Buchenwald'" 1945-04-15 Murrow's searing, unsparing eyewitness radio dispatch from the concentration camp.
Murrow_I_Can_Hear_It_Now.mp3 "Edward R. Murrow: 'I Can Hear It Now - Fr. William Downey on V-E Day'" 1948-11-20 Retrospective audio documentary capturing the spiritual climax of V-E Day.
Welles_War_Bond_Plea.mp3 "Orson Welles: 'Wartime War Bond Plea & Home-Front Rally'" 1943-09-12 Powerful rhetorical appeal urging Americans to purchase war bonds.
Radio_Hamburg_Liberation.mp3 "Allied Military Government: 'Radio Hamburg Post-Liberation Broadcast & Interval'" 1945-05-04 The first Allied-controlled broadcast over northwest Germany's primary transmitter.
